subject: Tree cover loss in India, 2001 onwards — the satellite measurement
kind_note: Canopy change measured from Landsat imagery. It is a measurement, not a model. What it MEANS depends entirely on the definition of the threshold, which is why the threshold is stated everywhere the number is.

source.name: Hansen / University of Maryland tree cover loss, published by Global Forest Watch (World Resources Institute)

obtained_via.what_it_is: the keyless same-origin proxy that WRI's own Global Nature Watch web client uses to read these datasets
obtained_via.why: The documented API at data-api.globalforestwatch.org requires a key, which this build did not create. This proxy serves the identical dataset at a stated version.
obtained_via.honesty: This is a public web client's proxy, NOT a documented API contract. It can change or close without notice and it is not a licence. Every figure records the dataset and version so it is checkable against the authoritative source by anyone holding a key. Obtaining a key remains the right long-term answer.

threshold.why: GFW's own headline figures use 30 per cent. It is a CHOICE and a different choice gives a different answer, so it is printed wherever the number is.
threshold.semantics: cumulative nested subsets — the 10% figure INCLUDES the 30% figure
threshold.the_trap: Summing across thresholds double-counts and gives roughly eight times the real total. This job asserts the ladder is monotonically decreasing before it writes.

primary_forest.what_it_is: loss inside forest mapped as regional primary forest in 2001 — mature natural forest, the part that does not come back on a human timescale

planted_split.reading: The share of measured tree-cover loss that was NOT inside a planted forest. It is the answer to the commonest objection to this series — that it merely counts plantation harvests, which grow back.

caveats: Tree cover loss is not deforestation. It counts canopy disappearing for any reason — felling, fire, storm, disease, harvest — and it does not say why.
It is not net change. Gain is a separate measurement on a different method and the two are not subtracted from each other here.
The threshold changes the answer. Every figure states which threshold it is on.
A failed query is recorded as null, never as zero loss.
This series and India's own forest report measure different things and disagree. Both are published. Neither is averaged into the other.
